== Biography ==
{{Ireland Native}}
{{Migrating Ancestor
|origin=Ireland
|destination=United States
|origin-flag=Ireland_Flags.png
|destination-flag=Flags-1.png
}}

'''Alexander Glasgow''' was born in northern Ireland in 1786, although some family information gives his birth year as 1788. Find a Grave records a more precise birth date of 26 February 1786.<ref name="FindAGrave">"Alexander Glasgow," Find a Grave, memorial no. 54173175, born 26 February 1786; died 4 December 1855; citing Pine Creek Cemetery, Allison Park, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, USA; https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/54173175/alexander-glasgow</ref>

Alexander's gravestone does not state his birth date directly. It records that he died on 4 December 1855, aged 69 years, 9 months and 8 days. That age calculates to a birth date of 26 February 1786.<ref name="FindAGrave">{{FindAGrave|54173175}}</ref>

The calculated date conflicts with the reported birth of his presumed brother [[Glasgow-539|Hugh Glasgow]] on 25 July 1786. Hugh was also reportedly a twin. The conflict has not been resolved and may concern one of the birth dates, the stated sibling relationship, or the identification of one of the men.

Alexander came from a Scots-Irish family. His parents were [[Glasgow-540|Hugh Glasgow]] and [[Blair-3693|Sarah Blair]].<ref name="GlasgowFamilyHistory">William Melanchthon Glasgow, ''Family History Document''; https://www.wikitree.com/photo/pdf/Glasgow-590</ref>

The Glasgow family immigrated to the United States after Alexander's birth, probably sometime during the 1790s. By 1810, Hugh Glasgow and his family had settled in Deer Township, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania.

The existing research notes describe Alexander as married and living on a farm of his own at the time of the 1810 census.<ref name="USCensus1810">"United States Census, 1810," database with images, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XH2K-Z8X : accessed 25 May 2020), Alexr Glasgow, Deer, Allegheny, Pennsylvania, United States; citing p. 314, NARA microfilm publication M252 (Washington, D.C.: National Archives and Records Administration, n.d.), roll 44; FHL microfilm 193,670.</ref> He remained in Deer Township in 1830.<ref name="USCensus1830">"United States Census, 1830," database with images, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XHP6-D5M : 22 August 2017), Alexander Glasgow, Deer, Allegheny, Pennsylvania, United States; citing p. 347, NARA microfilm publication M19 (Washington, D.C.: National Archives and Records Administration, n.d.), roll 144; FHL microfilm 20,618.</ref> By 1840, he was recorded as Alex Glascow in West Deer Township.<ref name="USCensus1840">"United States Census, 1840," database with images, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XHBQ-PD6 : 19 May 2020), Alex Glascow, West Deer Township, Allegheny, Pennsylvania, United States; citing p. 73. The NARA roll and FHL microfilm numbers were not supplied in the original citation.</ref>

The 1850 census lists a woman named Sarah in Alexander's household. She was recorded as one year younger than Alexander and was presumably his wife.<ref name="USCensus1850">"United States Census, 1850," database with images, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M448-X12 : 4 April 2020), Alex Glasgow, West Deer, Allegheny, Pennsylvania, United States; citing family 114, NARA microfilm publication M432 (Washington, D.C.: National Archives and Records Administration, n.d.).</ref>

Alexander died on 4 December 1855 in West Deer Township, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania. He was buried in Pine Creek Cemetery in Allison Park, Pennsylvania.<ref name="FindAGrave" />

== Marriage ==

Alexander's wife is believed to have been '''Sarah''', possibly Sarah Taggart, although her surname remains uncertain.

Alexander and Sarah were the grandparents of the profile contributor's wife's second-great-grandfather, Robert C. Glasgow.

'''Identification warning:''' Alexander's wife is not the same person as Sarah Taggart, born in 1814, who married a different Alexander Glasgow—the son of Alexander's brother John.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-540]] is assessed at 95% (proved). The held family-history account explicitly names Hugh Glasgow and Sarah Blair as Alexander’s parents. Alexander’s 1786 generation fits their established Pennsylvania household and the named son group, giving a specific compiled-family identification.

Confident95%; family-history evidence, no newly inspected contemporary parent record.

Next useful test: Compare the named son entry with Hugh’s family and probate papers.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/photo/pdf/Glasgow-590 William Melanchthon Glasgow, Family History Document; https://www.wikitree.com/photo/pdf/Glasgow-590]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.
